subject: VelociTech: checkout latency & 5xx surge — RCA, actions, and follow-up

From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@velocitech.com>

Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-11-02T16:20:00Z
Subject: Severe latency spikes impacting checkout — urgent

Hi Irene / Karthik,

We hit sustained checkout latency and elevated 5xx rates this morning between 08:12-09:04 PT. Rough metrics: median latency for checkout increased from ~220ms to ~1.8s and checkout failures (5xx) spiked to ~4.6% of requests. This impacted a subset of customers on us-west-2 and caused a visible revenue drop for our B2C checkout.

We opened a PagerDuty incident (INC-42178). The VelociTech SRE team applied a short-term routing change to reduce impact but we'd like Redwood to provide:
- immediate RCA summary
- a remediation timeline and owners for permanent fixes
- confirmation on whether this is covered under our SLA and any credit steps

Can we get an exec-readout + action plan by EOD tomorrow? We’re looping our Head of Ops (Raj) on this thread.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Director, Platform Operations
VelociTech

Subject: VelociTech incident — preliminary RCA and immediate mitigations

Team / Olivia,

Summary (prelim):
- Root cause: a model-variant routing regression combined with a change in KV-cache TTLs that increased cold cache misses for higher-length checkout sequences. The regression originated in the model routing layer deployed in us-west-2 at 07:45 PT (release tag: routing-v2.9.1).
- Impact window: 07:52 — 09:05 PT.
- Visible symptoms: increased tail latency (p95/p99) and elevated 5xx caused by request queues saturating under higher token lengths.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Rolled back routing-v2.9.1 at 08:58 PT (deployment revert) — reduced error rate to baseline by ~08:59 PT.
- Temporarily increased KV-cache TTL to reduce cache misses for checkout keys (hotfix).

Deliverables and owners:
- Draft RCA (attached) — Marcus Lin (eng) — delivery Nov 3 EOD
- Permanent fix: routing-layer validation + deploy guardrails — Karthik Iyer (platform eng) — target Nov 10
- Cache rework: KV warmup strategy and TTL tuning with sims — Engineering (Marcus) + Product (Karthik) — target Nov 17
- SLA review and credit recommendation — Laura Bennett (revenue ops) — meet Nov 4

Attachments: velocitech_rca_draft.pdf, throughput_commitments.xlsx, pagerduty-INC-42178.log.txt

Notes: we are treating the rollback as a targeted mitigation, not the final fix. I’ll take point on adding a deploy-time check to prevent routing fallback to incompatible model variants.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Olivia / Raj —

Thank you for the patience while we dug into this. High-level for execs:
- What happened: model-routing regression + KV-cache TTL change caused transient cold-cache behavior and queue saturation in us-west-2.
- Customer impact: elevated checkout latency and ~4.6% failure rate for ~72 minutes.
- Immediate fixes: rollback of routing change + temporary TTL increase returned metrics to baseline.

Proposed near-term commitments from Redwood (agreeable to adjust):
1) By Nov 4 EOD: final RCA document + clear ownership list (Irene/Martus/Laura) — DONE target
2) By Nov 10: deploy-time validation for routing compatibility and rollback guardrails — owner: Karthik
3) By Nov 17: KV cache strategy & load testing to prevent cache-warm misses on long sequences — owner: Marcus
4) Weekly technical sync (30m) until completion — cadence: Wednesdays 09:00 PT; first sync Nov 10
5) SLA credit evaluation — Laura to propose credit amount by Nov 4 and share a draft credit note

Please confirm these commitments and let us know if you want executive-level slides for your C-suite. We can also add a formal postmortem call with engineering leaders if helpful.

Thanks — we’ll drive to closure and share status updates in the shared Drive link.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
